hits.tldr: Theme variables compile to CSS custom properties for use in stylesheets.
Tailwind CSS imports default theme variables for colors, fonts, shadows, and spacing via layer declarations.
Use the prefix option to namespace Tailwind CSS classes and variables to avoid naming conflicts.
Prefixed classes appear at the start of class names, theme variables are configured without prefix but generated CSS includes it.
Use the `inline` option when theme variables reference other variables to avoid CSS resolution issues.

content.text:
No, it isn't safe. Unprefixed `--color-*` variables in your shipped CSS can collide with variables on your users' sites. The docs don't address the library-distribution case directly, but they do give you a fix.

- Use the `prefix` option: `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);`. The docs say it namespaces "all Tailwind-generated classes and CSS variables". The compiled output then has `--tw-color-red-500` and `.tw\:text-red-500` (`styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Managing style conflicts → Using the prefix option").
- You still write `@theme` variables without the prefix (`--color-avocado-100`). The generated CSS adds it, which "avoid[s] conflicts with any existing variables in your project" (`upgrade-guide.mdx`, "Changes from v3 → Using a prefix").
- This keeps built-in utilities like `rounded-lg` working. Your classes become `tw:rounded-lg`, and you can pick any prefix you like. The docs don't say whether the prefix covers variables you add yourself in `@theme`, so check your compiled output.

- Use the `prefix` option: `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);`. The docs say it namespaces "all Tailwind-generated classes and CSS variables". The compiled output then has `--tw-color-red-500` and `.tw\:text-red-500` (`styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Managing style conflicts → Using the prefix option").
- You still write `@theme` variables without the prefix (`--color-avocado-100`). The generated CSS adds it, which "avoid[s] conflicts with any existing variables in your project" (`upgrade-guide.mdx`, "Changes from v3 → Using a prefix").
- This keeps built-in utilities like `rounded-lg` working. Your classes become `tw:rounded-lg`, and you can pick any prefix you like. The docs don't say whether the prefix covers variables you add yourself in `@theme`, so check your compiled output.
